extracted.intended_audience: attorneys authorized to practice before the USPTO; counsel in disciplinary proceedings; USPTO OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Administrative/disciplinary procedure under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 for imposing reciprocal discipline (suspension) on an individual authorized to practice before the USPTO based on state disciplinary action. Covers notice, opportunity to respond, default consequences, publication, and post-discipline duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for USPTO suspension (violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended for five years from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states: 'Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, Andrew S. Breines ... is hereby suspended for five years ... for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline based on state suspension on ethical grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline before the USPTO may be imposed predicated upon being suspended from the practice of law on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice text: '... ordered that Mr. Breines be suspended for five years ... for violating 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being indefinitely suspended from the practice of law on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State.' The action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to file a response within forty (40) days
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must send a 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' notifying the respondent and providing an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline based on the reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was sent by certified mail (receipt nos. listed) and 'provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline ... based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).' The Notice was delivered on March 17, 2018.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to file a timely response (default/no genuine issue)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline identical to the state-imposed discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis: 'In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is hereby determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and Respondent's suspension ... for five (5) years is the appropriate discipline.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements (Official Gazette and 37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish a Notice in the Official Gazette and give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to state disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts where the respondent is admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order paragraphs: 'The OED Director publish the following Notice in the Official Gazette...' and 'The OED Director give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-discipline duties (compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 following imposition of discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order paragraph: 'Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.' (The Order does not restate § 11.58 duties but requires compliance.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying misconduct findings (state-law ethical violations leading to discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Massachusetts Board of Bar Overseers charged violations of Massachusetts Rules of Professional Conduct 4.1(a), 8.4(c), and 8.4(h), and found failure to report a conviction to bar counsel; these state findings served as the predicate for the state suspension and thereby the USPTO reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice text: 'The Massachusetts Office of the Bar Counsel filed a formal complaint ... charging Mr. Breines with violations of Massachusetts Rules of Professional Conduct 4.1(a) (making a false statement of material fact or law to a third person), 8.4(c) (engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation) and 8.4(h) (engaging in any other conduct that adversely reflects on his fitness to practice law). Mr. Breines also failed to report the conviction of a crime to bar counsel.'
